label: <DEL> step of short sequences starting with j/n/0 (plus weak mid-original firing)
explanation: Sparse unit (about 1% of steps). About 65% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (7.3% of delimiter steps fire). Delimiter firing is much more likely, and the top activations are strongest, when the sequence starts with j (6.8x lift), n or 0 (then f/h/e/r), and when L is short (L 3-6); the largest examples also contain n or w early in the sequence. The remaining ~35% of mass is in the original phase at t=3-6, on first-occurrence inputs, most often l, v, s, 3, x, and frequently in the same sequences that later fire on <DEL>. It essentially never fires in the copy phase (0.3% of mass, only on the first output) or at t=0-1. The content dependence looks like a distributed readout of the stored prefix, not a single token rule: the best predicate (delimiter & first token in {j,n,0,f,h,e,r} & L<=6) gets dev F1 0.35, and adding an original-phase clause raises mass recall to 0.65 but lowers precision.
